workoff.income_limit: No income guidelines for the first qualified owner. A second qualifying owner may earn the exemption if they meet the need requirements.
workoff.signup_window: Open enrollment in October. The program year runs November 16 to the following November 15.
workoff.apply_where: SCRPT Program Coordinator, Elder Services / The Robb Center (Senior Center)
workoff.quote: The program runs from November 16 to the following November 15. Please check back in October for open enrollment. Contact Ashley for more information (978) 623-8320

exemption_41c.doubling_5c_half: The town says 'Initial amount is $1,000 per year; Maximum amount is $2,000 per year' but does not name 5C-1/2

asset_limits.note: whole estate, not counting the home unless it has 4+ apartments

exemption_41c.fiscal_year: FY2018 is the only dated town source. The current /693 page and the Assessor's statutory-exemptions PDF are undated but show identical figures.
exemption_41c.deadline: Applications should be filed with the Board of Assessors every year. No date is stated.
exemption_41c.quote: Must be at least 70 years old on or before July 1st. ... Annual gross receipts (income) cannot exceed: $20,000 if you are single $30,000 if you are married ... Initial amount is $1,000.00 per year. Maximum amount is $2,000.00 per year

other_senior_relief.name: Andover Means Tested Senior Tax Exemption (FY2027)
other_senior_relief.detail: Local exemption equal to 50-100% of the state Senior Circuit Breaker credit received on the 2025 MA return. Select Board sets the percentage each year. Eligibility: 65 by Dec 31, 2025 (a joint applicant can be 60+); owned and occupied the Andover home 10 years; assessed value no more than $1,172,000. APPLICATIONS DUE SEPTEMBER 30, 2026. Credited on the Feb 1 and May 1, 2027 bills.
other_senior_relief.quote: Completed applications are due to the Assessors' office no later than September 30, 2026. ... up to a 100 percent match and not less than a 50 percent match of the amount of the circuit breaker income tax credit

other_senior_relief.name: Clause 41A tax deferral
other_senior_relief.detail: Age 65+. Can defer the entire bill, up to 50% of the property's value, at 5% interest, with a lien repaid when released. Gross receipts must not exceed $40,000. Source undated; figures match the FY2018 chart.
other_senior_relief.quote: D. Must have gross receipts from all sources in preceding year not exceeding $40,000. ... This deferred amount incurs interest at 5%, payable with the deferred amount on release of a lien filed against your property.

other_senior_relief.name: Clause 17D exemption (age 70+ / surviving spouse / minor child)
other_senior_relief.detail: $175 initial, up to $350 per year. Whole estate must not exceed $40,000. Undated; figures match the FY2018 chart.
other_senior_relief.quote: Initial amount is $175.00 per year. Maximum amount is $350.00 per year.

other_senior_relief.name: Elderly and Disabled Tax Fund
other_senior_relief.detail: The town has a committee page for this fund, but the rendered page body shows no program details, eligibility or contact. Only the page's own summary line could be verified.
other_senior_relief.quote: The Elderly Tax Aid helps seniors who can't pay their taxes.
